title: Ines and the Witness
premise: Mara Underhill, a night-shift dispatcher who treats every case like a puzzle to be closed, is paid a small fortune by a nervous client to prove that a murder scheduled for the night of the citywide blackout never happened. Digging through cab logs, radio chatter, and dead-end streets, Mara discovers the 'victim' may still be alive — and that the only person who saw everything is the witness the prosecution insists is dead. As the trial date closes in and Mara's own name starts appearing in places he never drove, he realizes his client hired him not to find the truth but to bury it. Choosing loyalty to the truth over the safety of invisibility, Mara finds the witness hiding in plain sight inside the taxi company itself, testifies at the cost of his anonymity, and finally belongs somewhere — to the truth.
about_author: Oscar Lockridge spent a decade driving night cabs in a city that never told him its real name, collecting the stories passengers left behind like fare receipts. He writes mysteries from the passenger seat of memory, where every street corner hides a confession.

chapters.title: The Advance Payment
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A cash-stuffed envelope arrives with a single instruction: prove the murder of councilman's aide Daniel Reyes hasn't happened yet. Mara, who never takes a case he can't close, accepts against his better instincts. The emotional beat is the thrill of a puzzle — and the first prickle of unease when the client refuses to give a name.

chapters.title: Night Routes
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Working the dispatch board, Mara reconstructs every cab movement on the night Reyes supposedly died. The logs show a car that shouldn't exist — unit 47, retired two years ago, logged on the route that night. The beat is quiet dread: the city Mara thought he knew has seams.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The official witness, Lena Voss, died in a car crash months ago; the trial hinges on her testimony. But a diner waitress mentions a woman with Lena's scarred hands ordering coffee at 3 a.m. every Thursday. Hope flickers — and Mara realizes someone is following him home.

chapters.title: The Client's Voice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The anonymous client calls, furious that Mara is asking about Lena Voss instead of confirming the murder. The threat in his voice reframes everything: Mara wasn't hired to find truth, but to manufacture a clean record. The beat is betrayal — loyalty to a client he's never met versus loyalty to what he now knows.

chapters.title: Blackout
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara tracks unit 47's last driver, an old-timer named Sal, who confesses he drove a terrified Lena Voss out of the city the night of the blackout — and was paid by someone at the taxi company to forget. The company Mara belongs to is inside the plot. The beat is vertigo: home is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Fare
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following Sal's route, Mara finds Daniel Reyes alive, hiding in a flophouse — the 'victim' staged his own death to escape a corruption scheme, and the client is the councilman who wants the record sealed before trial. Reyes begs Mara to stay invisible. The beat is temptation: closing the case means walking away.

chapters.title: Thursday, 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara stakes out the diner and finally meets Lena Voss, very much alive, protected by Sal and the night-shift drivers who've been feeding her for months. She's terrified to testify; the drivers are loyal to her, not to Mara. The beat is belonging — Mara, the invisible man, is suddenly trusted with something real.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The client's men burn the dispatch office, and Sal is hospitalized shielding Lena's location. Mara's boss reveals the councilman owns the company's debts — everyone Mara loves is leverage. The beat is the theme made flesh: loyalty to people now demands the truth, and the truth will cost them all.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Back Seat
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, climax. On the trial's eve, the councilman's men corner Mara and Reyes; Mara's only escape is the one move nobody expects — driving straight to the courthouse with Lena in the back seat, radioing the whole night shift to run interference. Cabs swarm the streets as cover. The beat is triumph through solidarity: the invisible network made visible.

chapters.title: Fare Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Lena testifies, Reyes takes the stand, and the councilman's scheme unravels. Mara, once defined by staying unseen, gives his name in open court. The company survives under new ownership; Sal recovers; the night shift saves Mara a seat. The beat is resolution: he closed the only case that mattered — the one on his own invisibility.
